strapiBlog.title: Dubai to Transform Jebel Ali Racecourse into Walkable Island-Inspired District
strapiBlog.short_description: Plans are underway to dramatically reshape the grounds of Dubai's famed Jebel Ali Racecourse, turning the site into a walkable island-inspired community.

data.text:
Plans are underway to dramatically reshape the grounds of Dubai's famed Jebel Ali Racecourse, turning the site into a walkable island-inspired community. This development will introduce a series of residential islands, lush green corridors, and integrated public amenities—all part of an ambitious new approach to urban living.

Here's everything you need to know about the Jebel Ali Racecourse transformation master plan.

Legacy of Champions: A Look Back at Jebel Ali Racecourse

Before its transformation into a Dubai green walkable district, Jebel Ali Racecourse was the beating heart of equestrian culture in the city. Built in 1990, it attracted iconic figures like British jockey Lester Piggott.

Over the decades, it has hosted more than 70 races annually and continues to welcome thousands of spectators each season. The legacy of the racecourse is intricately tied to Dubai's global ascent in the world of horse racing, with its success paving the way for major events like the Dubai World Cup.

About Jebel Ali Racecourse Transformation Master Plan

The Jebel Ali Racecourse transformation is part of a broader initiative under the Dubai urban masterplan 2025. It aims to reshape the emirate's landscape in response to growing population needs.

Spread over 5 sq. km., the new development will preserve the historic racecourse while layering in equestrian venues, cultural spaces, mixed-use buildings, and sustainable living zones—making it one of the most visionary urban projects in the city.

data.text:
Design by Visionaries: BIG Bjarke Ingels Dubai Project

Led by internationally acclaimed design firm BIG (Bjarke Ingels Group) in partnership with A.R.M. Holding, this Dubai development exemplifies cutting-edge thinking.

Described as an "archipelago of urban islands in a sea of green," the Jebel Ali Racecourse redevelopment project seeks to blur the line between natural landscapes and urban infrastructure. A central green spine—a large public park—will serve as the community's heart, anchored by shaded pedestrian zones and eco-conscious planning.

Key Features of the Jebel Ali Racecourse Redevelopment Project

The upcoming district surrounding the Jebel Ali Racecourse is being designed with people, nature, and movement in mind. Built on the principles of sustainable urban development in Dubai is increasingly embracing this master-planned community, which will prioritize easy, car-free connectivity.

Let's take a look at the key features:

  • Walkable residential blocks, designed for comfort and convenience
  • Shaded communal plazas and pedestrian-friendly streets
  • Dedicated cycling lanes throughout the district
  • Autonomous shuttles providing last-mile connectivity
  • Seamless integration with public transportation networks

Supporting the Dubai 2040 Vision

The Jebel Ali Racecourse redevelopment plays a critical role in achieving the goals of the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan. The vision of a '20-minute city'—where most daily needs are accessible within 20 minutes on foot or bicycle—takes centre stage here.

This vision is reinforced by projects like the Dubai Walk Master Plan, which adds 3,000 km of pedestrian walkways and 112 km of waterfront paths to the city.

While the Jebel Ali Racecourse transformation stands out for its scale and vision, it joins a series of mega developments shaping Dubai's urban future. Expo City Dubai, for example, is evolving into a powerhouse of innovation and entrepreneurship.

Likewise, Palm Jebel Ali is being revived with plans to offer beachside living to 35,000 families, supported by 80 resorts and hotels. These projects, like the one at Jebel Ali, reinforce Dubai's commitment to holistic, sustainable growth.

faqs.question: What is the Jebel Ali Racecourse redevelopment project?

data.answer: It is a large-scale urban development plan to transform the area around Jebel Ali Racecourse into a walkable, green district with residential islands, parks, and cultural venues.

faqs.question: Who is leading the Jebel Ali Racecourse transformation?

data.answer: The project is led by BIG (Bjarke Ingels Group) and A.R.M. Holding.

faqs.question: Will the original Jebel Ali Racecourse be preserved?

data.answer: Yes, the racecourse will remain intact and integrated into the new urban district as a central heritage feature.

faqs.question: How does this project support sustainable urban development in Dubai?

data.answer: The project incorporates green spaces, walkability, smart mobility solutions, and eco-conscious design principles in line with Dubai's sustainability goals.

faqs.question: When will construction of the Jebel Ali Racecourse redevelopment begin?

data.answer: Construction is expected to commence early next year, with the development happening in phases.

faqs.question: What transportation options will be available in the new district?

data.answer: The development will feature pedestrian paths, cycling lanes, and self-driving shuttles for easy access to public transport.
